prompt:
Architecture ticket. Design the deployable target state for our new CHI01 VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 site and the ordered move from the estate that it replaces. This is an architecture deliverable, not a prose recommendation.

Research before editing: use your real network research tools to consult current, publicly reachable Broadcom-published VMware Cloud Foundation compatibility/interoperability and upgrade-path material. Pay particular attention to the documented behavior when an installed component build is chronologically newer than the build in the selected VCF bundle. Do not treat the local compatibility snapshot as research. Record the exact page titles and HTTPS URLs you actually consulted, plus what each informed, in `researchSources` in the artifact. Each entry must have a nonempty `title`, `url`, and nonempty `consultedFor` string array. Make the recorded research cover compatibility or interoperability, upgrade sequencing or paths, and the newer-installed-build restriction. You may choose the sources and queries; do not assume that any particular live page is stable.

The protected inputs are `fixtures/design_requirements.json`, `fixtures/estate_inventory.json`, `fixtures/compatibility_snapshot.json`, `schemas/migration-plan.schema.json`, and `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json`. The installer document is the unmodified Apache-2.0 file from tag `9.1.0.0` of `vmware/vcf-api-specs`. The compatibility snapshot, not the mutable live matrix, is the deterministic authority for the migration plan. Leave those inputs and `verifier_test.go` unchanged.

Implement package `architecture` at the module root and complete `BuildArchitecture(requirementsPath, inventoryPath, compatibilityPath string) ([]byte, error)`. Add table-driven Go tests. `BuildArchitecture` must return a JSON object with `sddcSpec`, `migrationPlan`, and `researchSources`; its `sddcSpec` and `migrationPlan` must be semantically identical to the checked-in `architecture.json`.

`architecture.json` is the machine-checkable deliverable. Its `sddcSpec` must be a greenfield `SddcSpec` that validates as `#/components/schemas/SddcSpec` in the pinned installer OpenAPI document and implements the capacity, host-failure tolerance, appliance availability, site services, naming, and network requirements in the design fixture. Do not import or reuse the existing estate in that spec, and use an obvious non-secret placeholder wherever the installer schema requires a password. A password placeholder must contain at least one of these plainly recognizable markers: `CHANGE_ME`, `CHANGE-ME`, `CHANGEME`, `PLACEHOLDER`, `EXAMPLE`, `DUMMY`, `NOT_A_SECRET`, or `NOT-A-SECRET`. Include the VCF 9.1 management-services infrastructure, VCF Operations HA deployment, and license server required by the fixture.

Its `migrationPlan` must validate against `schemas/migration-plan.schema.json`, use the `parallel-greenfield` strategy, and contain one ordered step for every component in the estate inventory. Each step must name the component, exact current version/build, exact destination target, action, and all technical gates dictated by the compatibility snapshot. Preserve the snapshot's order. A transition marked unsupported because the installed build is newer than the target bundle must never be represented as an in-place upgrade; use the snapshot's replacement action and gates. Do not add components that are absent from the inventory.

Run `go test -race -timeout 60s ./...` until it passes.

research.interface: Broadcom compatibility, interoperability, and VCF upgrade-path publications
research.language_rationale: The deliverable is generated and verified as typed JSON by a Go package; race-enabled table-driven tests make the architecture and migration ordering deterministic.
